names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 6 februarie, «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan din Gaza». The life the site prints for him heads him «Ioan Profetul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 6 Φεβρουαρίου, «Όσιοι Βαρσανούφιος και Ιωάννης ο μαθητής του ο επικαλούμενος Προφήτης», with the rank word and the epithets left off.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 6 февраля ст. ст., «Иоанн пророк, прп.», with the rank word and the office left off. «пророк» stands here as the epithet by which the calendar tells him apart and not as a rank, so it is kept in the form.

floruit.note: doxologia.ro's life: «Sfântul Varsanufie cel Mare și Ioan Profetul au trăit în timpul secolului al VI-lea, în timpul domniei împăratului Iustinian I (483-565).» The same page says he lived in his cell «începând cu anii 524-525 … timp de 18 ani până la moartea sa», but prints no year for his death.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 6 февраля ст. ст. — «Прпп. Варсонофия Великого и Иоанна Пророка (VI).»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 6 februarie — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan din Gaza»

attestations.note: The day prints him and Barsanuphius the Great as two lines over one and the same life. The site's hymn page for the two of them is a video recording and prints no text but a refrain, so no hymn is recorded here.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 6ης Φεβρουαρίου — «Όσιοι Βαρσανούφιος και Ιωάννης ο μαθητής του ο επικαλούμενος Προφήτης»

attestations.note: Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).
